SEARCH

Package hadur2

package hadur2
The Robocode adapter: the only code in Hadur 2 that sees the engine.

The architecture is hexagonal. All strategy lives in hadur2.core, which imports nothing from robocode.* (CORE-1) and sees only plain values. This package is the thin shell around it:

  • Hadur is the robot. Each engine event handler (onScannedRobot, onHitByBullet, ...) turns the event into a BotEvent and queues it; each turn the run loop reads the getters into a BotInput with the queued events, passes it to the core through Guard, and turns the returned BotOrders back into setTurnRightRadians, setAhead, setMaxVelocity, setTurnGunRightRadians, setTurnRadarRightRadians and setFire calls before execute(). A NaN order leaves that setting alone and a fire power of 0 holds fire. Angles pass through unchanged in radians, Robocode's convention (0 = north, clockwise); distances are in px.
  • FileProfileStore is the ProfileStore port on the robot's data directory, where opponent profiles live between battles.
  • HadurRecorder is the robot plus a transcript of every input and order in hadur2.core.replay's line format, for replay fixtures (CORE-2). It is left out of the competition jar.

Faults (RES-1)

The adapter never calls the core directly: every tick goes through Guard.tick(hadur2.core.model.BotInput), which catches anything the core throws (or a null result), records the fault, and returns the safe order set for that tick (full speed on the current direction of travel, body side-on to the enemy's last bearing, hold fire, radar on that bearing or sweeping). The adapter applies those orders like any others, so the robot keeps moving and scanning while the core is down.

Java version (REL-1)

The module is compiled for Java 11 (the build's maven.compiler.release), like the core it shades in, because RoboRumble clients run whatever Java their owners installed. Main code therefore avoids records, sealed types and pattern matching; Path.of, which the recorder uses, is Java 11 API.

Robocode's sandbox and the profile files (RES-3)

Robocode runs a robot under a security manager. A robot may read files in its own data directory, but may write only through robocode.RobocodeFileOutputStream, only inside that directory, and only within its data quota; renaming a file is punished. So the usual crash-safe "write a temporary file, then rename it over the old one" is not available. Instead the core's ProfileLibrary writes the temporary copy, then the profile, then deletes the copy, and a load takes whichever passes its checksum (RES-3); FileProfileStore only moves bytes. Robocode also charges the quota for bytes written and refunds a file's length only when it is reopened for writing, so the store empties a file through the stream before deleting it.

File work happens at safe moments: the profile store is set up and the battle clock read in run() before the first tick, a profile is loaded at the first scan (MEM-1), and it is saved in onRoundEnded while the robot is alive and in onBattleEnded (MEM-3), never in onWin or onDeath.

This package may use robocode.*, java.io and the clock (System.nanoTime, to measure the core's tick for TIME-1); the ArchUnit rules that forbid them apply to hadur2.core only.
